questions: Does the cost of swapping P_i and P_{i+1} depend on the current values at those positions, or is it always exactly i regardless of what values are swapped?
Is the goal to sort P into strictly increasing order (1,2,...,N), or could it be non-decreasing order (allowing duplicates)?
Can we choose any sequence of swaps, or must we follow a specific algorithm (like bubble sort) to minimize cost?
If multiple minimal-cost sequences exist, does the output require the minimal cost value, or could it be any sequence's cost?
Are we allowed to perform swaps that temporarily increase inversion count if they lead to lower overall cost?
Does the cost accumulate per swap operation (pay i each time), or is it a one-time fee for choosing i as an allowed swap index?
Is the cost i based on the original fixed indices 1..N-1, or does it shift as elements move (i.e., cost based on current positions of values)?
Should the output be the minimal possible total cost over all sequences of swaps that sort P, or just the cost of a specific described procedure?
